title: The dream that fades by breakfast
text: {{1}} dreams evaporate so quickly is still debated, but the chemistry is suggestive: while we sleep, noradrenaline, {{2}} helps lock memories in, {{3}} in short supply, and the dreaming brain may simply be unable to file its own product. What is clear is that the window closes fast: {{4}} first minutes after waking are critical, and by breakfast most of the night's cinema has been demolished. {{5}} helps to write the dream down immediately, {{6}} the bed, before analysis or even movement gets in the way. People who keep dream journals report longer, more vivid dreams within weeks — {{7}} the dreams change or the attention does is happily unclear. {{8}} a notebook by the bed turns out to be, in effect, a memory aid for a department of the mind that otherwise keeps no records.
